questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the minimum required fields on a standard invoice header?
questions.explain: Bank/branch details live on the supplier's bank account record, not as a required field on the invoice header itself.

questions.q: What does the 'Invoice Number' field on a standard invoice actually represent?
options: The number the supplier themselves printed on their bill
questions.explain: The invoice number is whatever the supplier assigned to their own bill, which is why it must be entered accurately.

questions.q: Why does Payables check for duplicate invoice numbers per supplier?
options: To determine the invoice's approval routing
As a control against entering and potentially paying the same invoice twice
questions.explain: Checking for a duplicate invoice number under the same supplier helps catch accidental or fraudulent double entry/payment.

questions.q: What happens when you select a supplier site while creating an invoice?
options: Nothing defaults in; everything must be typed manually
The invoice number is automatically generated by Fusion
Payment terms and default address information default in from the site, but can still be overridden on the invoice
questions.explain: Site-level defaults like payment terms fill in automatically but remain editable on an individual invoice.

questions.q: What happens immediately after a standard invoice header and its lines are saved?
options: The invoice still needs to pass validation before it can move toward approval and payment
The supplier is automatically merged with another supplier
questions.explain: Saving an invoice is separate from validating it — validation is still required before approval and payment can proceed.
